It includes, but is not limited to, fourwheel drive or low-pressure-tire vehicles, motorcycles, and related two-wheel vehicles, snowmobiles, amphibious machines, ground-effect or air-cushion vehicles, recreation vehicle campers, and any other means of transportation deriving motive power from any source other than muscle. Exceptions include any registered motorboat; any military, fire, emergency, or law enforcement vehicle while being used for official or emergency purposes; farm type tractors and other self-propelled agricultural equipment when used exclusively for agricultural purposes; any self-propelled equipment for harvesting and transportation of forest products or for earth moving or construction while being used for these purposes; self-propelled lawn mowers, snowblowers, garden or lawn tractors, and golf carts while being used exclusively for their designed purpose; mining, oil, and gas geophysical exploration equipment as provided for under specific provisions in Department's regulations governing off-road vehicles and any vehicle whose use is expressly authorized by the respective agency head under a permit, lease, license, or contract.
(ii) Public Lands
Any lands administered by the respective bureaus within the Department of the Interior.
(iii) Bureaus
National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, and Bureau of Reclamation within the Department of the Interior.
(iv) Authorized Officer
An employee of the respective bureau to whom has been delegated the authority to take actions under the established ORV regulations and powers related thereto.
b) Use Criteria (except for official use):
(i) Areas and trails shall be located to minimize damage to soil, watershed, vegetation, or other resources of the public lands.
(ii) Area and trails shall be located to minimize harassment of wildlife or significant disruption of wildlife habitats.
(iii) Areas and trails shall be located to minimize conflicts between ORV use and other existing recreational uses of the same or neighboring public lands, and to ensure the compatibility of such uses with existing conditions in populated areas, taking into account noise and other factors.
